one_liner: Closure-derived int64/uint64 class for JavaScript; a tiny hand-written WebAssembly module beats its own float-based JS fallback on mul, div and rem.
what_it_does: Represents a 64-bit two's-complement value as an immutable Long object (signed low and high 32-bit halves plus an unsigned flag), with arithmetic, bitwise ops, shifts, rotates, comparisons, radix string conversion and, where the engine has BigInt, fromBigInt/toBigInt. The API is method-based (a.mul(b).shru(3)), and every operation returns a new Long. The fast path is chosen automatically: callers see the same API whether or not WebAssembly is available. It ships as one dependency-free ESM file with a UMD build and TypeScript types (npm 'long', used by protobufjs).
how_it_is_fast: At import, index.js synchronously instantiates an inline module of about 200 bytes (source in wasm.wat) that exports mul, div_s, div_u, rem_s, rem_u and get_high. Each export rebuilds an i64 from the two 32-bit halves, runs one native i64.mul, i64.div or i64.rem, returns the low half, and leaves the high half in a mutable Wasm global that JS reads with get_high(). This replaces the Closure Library algorithms: a 16-bit-limb schoolbook multiply, and a division loop that approximates rem/divisor in doubles and corrects downward, with modulo computed as this - (this/d)*d. Add, subtract, shifts and comparisons stay in JS.
when_to_use: Exact wrapping int64/uint64 arithmetic in JavaScript where BigInt is unavailable, disallowed, or not what an API expects (protobufjs and Closure-style code pass Long objects).
Division- and remainder-heavy 64-bit work (ID and hash arithmetic, 64-bit decoders) in engines with WebAssembly: about 10-19x faster than the forced JS fallback in the enricher's Node 22 run.
Code that needs direct access to the low and high 32-bit words, or must run unchanged in browsers, Node, Deno and older engines with automatic fallback.
when_not_to_use: Modern-only targets: native BigInt with BigInt.asIntN/asUintN took 0.6-1.1x the Wasm path's time per op in the enricher run, and it needs no library or Long allocations.
Pages with a strict CSP that blocks WebAssembly compilation (issue #58), or engines without Wasm: it silently falls back to JS, which was 3.5x (mul) to 19x (mod) slower in the enricher run.
Node 16.1+ on ARMv6: the import-time Wasm probe crashed the process instead of throwing (issue #107, closed as not planned).
Signed division by -1 of values near MIN_VALUE, or code that catches Error from mod(0): see gotchas.
Allocation-sensitive hot loops: each op creates a new Long object, and there are no in-place or mutable variants (issue #88's 'Q' variant proposal was not merged).

integration.min_toolchain: ES5-level JavaScript for the fallback; WebAssembly MVP with synchronous new WebAssembly.Module for the fast path; BigInt only for fromBigInt/toBigInt (added when typeof BigInt === 'function')
integration.platforms: any JavaScript engine (browsers, Node.js, Deno, Bun); the Wasm path needs Wasm compilation to be allowed
integration.thread_safety: Long values are immutable; each realm or worker gets its own Wasm instance, whose mutable 'high' global is read immediately after each call, so it is safe in ordinary single-threaded JS (from source, not documented)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the Wasm path and the JS fallback share one API and are selected automatically at load, but the Wasm path returns a different result for signed x.div(-1) when x is within 2^32 of MIN_VALUE, and throws a different error type for mod(0)

gotchas: Correctness bug on the Wasm path, which is the default in every current engine. The signed-division overflow guard tests this.high === -0x80000000 and divisor === -1 but not this.low === 0, so x.div(-1) returns x unchanged for all 2^32 signed values from MIN_VALUE to MIN_VALUE + 2^32 - 1. For example, Long.fromBits(5, 0x80000000).div(-1) gives -9223372036854775803 instead of 9223372036854775803. The JS fallback is correct. Reproduced with 5.3.2 HEAD on Node v22.22.0; tests/index.js does not cover it and no issue has been filed.

modulo() has no zero-divisor check on the Wasm path: x.mod(0) throws WebAssembly.RuntimeError 'remainder by zero', whereas div(0) and the JS fallback throw Error 'division by zero'. 20,000 random signed operand pairs otherwise matched BigInt on both paths for mul, div and mod.

The Wasm probe runs at import time. Under a CSP that blocks Wasm compilation it reports a violation and falls back (issue #58). Node 12 on Apple M1 died with 'wasm code commit Allocation failed' (issue #95, fixed by newer Node), and ARMv6 with Node 16.1+ hits a V8 trap (issue #107).
Mixing the ESM and CommonJS builds yields two different Long classes (README). isLong() checks the __isLong__ brand, so values still interoperate, but instanceof does not.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick long.js when you need a complete int64/uint64 value type in plain JavaScript with automatic Wasm acceleration and fallback. wasm-i128-div-bench is a 128-bit reciprocal-division technique for Rust-compiled Wasm, and galois targets finite-field arithmetic through AssemblyScript; neither is a general 64-bit integer type.
verified_claims_summary: The README says only that 'slow operations like division are around twice as fast' with the Wasm module, with no code, engine or hardware. A third-party run in issue #88 (Node v10.20.1, AMD Threadripper 2950X, 10M iterations x 10, Wasm vs --no-expose-wasm, benchmark file attached to the issue) measured an xor+mul+add+shr+sub chain at 89.57 vs 170.53 ns (1.9x) and the same chain plus div at 125.41 vs 589.22 ns (4.7x; the div step alone is about 36 vs 419 ns, about 11.7x, derived from page data). An enricher run (Node v22.22.0, Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz VM, 200,000 random operand pairs, median of 7, fallback forced by nulling the Wasm instance) measured mul 3.5x, div 10-16x and mod 13-19x over the JS fallback, with BigInt + asIntN at 0.6-1.1x the Wasm path's time. So the README understates the gain on current V8.
status_note: Stale but stable: npm 5.3.2 (2025-04-17) is the last release (143 commits, 918 stars, one open feature request). It is Apache-2.0, one dependency-free file, and widely depended on (about 4M weekly npm downloads per a 2022 comment in issue #107). The Wasm-path div(-1) bug near MIN_VALUE is unreported upstream.
